components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific of the pet owner (MR, MRS, MS or DR). When supplied it
            prefixes the composed 'salutation' (see Owner). Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          maxLength: 3
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted as a flat single-line value for
            backward compatibility; when the structured 'addressLine1'/'addressLine2' fields
            are supplied they take precedence. Returned as the composed, normalized address:
            the normalized 'addressLine1' with a single space and the normalized
            'addressLine2' appended when an 'addressLine2' is present, otherwise the
            normalized flat value.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the owner's structured postal address. When a non-blank value
            is supplied it is preferred over the flat 'address' input, and everything derived
            from the address uses the structured fields. Normalized like 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the owner's structured postal address (e.g. a unit
            or apartment). When present it is normalized and appended to the composed
            'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; validated only when present. When
            supplied it must be valid for the owner's city per the fixed region table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region
            accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it defaults
            to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth. Optional. When supplied it is used to
            derive the owner's 'ageBand' (see Owner) as of their registrationDate.
            Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true on create, allows registering an owner that shares a household
            (same last name and address) with an existing owner, bypassing the
            household-duplicate rejection. Write-only; never returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object

## Summary

The spec required `riskFlag` to be `true` on the owner read response when **any** of three signals hold: possible duplicate, disposable-adjacent email domain, or city over its soft capacity — otherwise `false`.

In this codebase the `POST /api/owners` pipeline already persists two of these signals onto the `Owner` entity (`possibleDuplicate` via `FlagOwnerPossibleDuplicate`, `capacityWarning` — the "soft capacity" band of 40–49 — via `FlagOwnerCityCapacity`), and `riskFlag` is a read-time derived field, so I computed it in the mapper alongside the other derived fields.

Changes:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a `riskFlag` boolean (`readOnly`) property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gains the field. Description mirrors the spec's three conditions.

2. **`DisposableEmailDomains.java`** (new) — a small helper holding the disposable blocklist with `isBlocked(email)` and `isDisposableAdjacent(email)`. "Disposable-adjacent" means the domain shares a blocked domain's registrable base label — same second-level name under any TLD, or a subdomain of a blocked domain (e.g. `mailinator.net`, `x.mailinator.com` for the blocked `mailinator.com`). Exactly-blocked domains count as adjacent too; absent/malformed emails are not.

3. **`ValidateOwnerEmailDomain.java`** — refactored to reuse `DisposableEmailDomains.isBlocked(...)` so the blocklist has a single source of truth. Behavior is unchanged (still rejects exact blocked domains with 400; leaves absent/blank untouched).

4. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — added `@Mapping(target = "riskFlag", ...)` and a `riskFlag(Owner)` method: `possibleDuplicate || disposableAdjacent || capacityWarning`, each null-safe via `Boolean.TRUE.equals(...)`.

Tests: `./mvnw -o test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`. The `coreRiskFlagFalseNormally` acceptance test (a fully-unique owner with no email, unique city, no duplicate) correctly returns `riskFlag: false`.

One design note worth surfacing: since a saved owner can never carry an *exactly*-blocked disposable domain (those are rejected with 400 at create time), the disposable-adjacent read-time signal only ever fires on the *related* variants (subdomains / alternate TLDs), which is why I implemented it as base-label matching rather than an exact-list lookup.
